full_judgment: 2. The subject matter of the pre-emption case is 6 decimals of land out of 39 decimals in Plot No. 14769 appertaining to R.S. Khatian No. 1987 of Mouza Middle Madrasha within P.S. Hat Hazari, District, Chittagong. The petitioners and opposite party Nos. 2-8 are co-sharers of the R.S. holding in question. By registered kabala dated 25-7-77, the opposite party Nos. 2-8 sold the case land to opposite party No. 1, who is a stranger purchaser. The possession of the land, however, remained with opposite party Nos. 2-8. By a contemporaneous registered agreement dated 25-7-77, the opposite party No. 1 agreed to recovery the land to the opposite party Nos. 2-8 on receipt back of the consideration money. On 2-11-77 the petitioners filed the application for pre-emption on depositing the consideration together with statutory compensation. By registered kabala dated 16-8-78, the opposite party No. 1 reconvened the case land to the opposite party Nos. 2-8 on receipt back of the consideration. The Trial Court took the view that the sale dated 25-7-77 coupled with the agreement for reconveyance dated the same constituted a mortgage and as such it dismissed the application for pre-emption. On appeal, the appellate court also affirmed the view of the Trial court that the two transactions namely the transaction of sale and the contract of re-conveyance taken together constituted mortgage and affirmed the decision of the Trial court. Both the courts below found and it has also been admitted in this court that the case land has already been re-conveyed by registered sale-deed dated 16-8-78 during the pendency of the pre-emption case. Being aggrieved by the decisions of the courts below the petitioners have moved this court and obtained the present rule.
